When benchmarked against other open source LLMs, Mistral V7 consistently ranks higher in performance, particularly in tasks requiring deep reasoning and nuanced language understanding.

Mistral AI continues its commitment to open source by releasing Mistral V7 under permissive licenses. Mistral V7 stands as a testament to the rapid progress in open source LLMs. Its state-of-the-art performance in coding, mathematics, and multilingual reasoning sets a new benchmark for what is possible in the open source domain. By making this model available to the community, Mistral AI not only advances the field of AI but also empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what can be achieved with language models. # Mistral AI 7B v0.1: Open Weight and Open Source

###### Abstract

We introduce Mistral AI 7B v0.1, an open-weight, open-source language model that performs on par with closed, state-of-the-art models, such as GPT-3.5, on a wide range of benchmarks. Mistral AI 7B v0.1 is a dense model, using only 8 billion parameters, and has been designed with the goal of providing high performance at a low computational cost. We focus on providing high-quality and factually accurate outputs, and we avoid generating harmful content, such as hateful or prejudiced language. Our model is also capable of following instructions, which makes it a useful tool for a variety of applications. Mistral AI 7B v0.1 is the first model released by Mistral AI, and we have made the weights and source code publicly available so that the community can build, study, and improve upon it. We hope that our model will be used to advance the field of open-source language models and provide a valuable resource for researchers and developers.

## 1 Introduction

The field of open-source language models has seen significant progress in the past year, with models like Llama *(Touvron et al., 2023)*, Vicuna *(Chiang et al., 2023)*, and OpenLLaMA *(Geng et al., 2023)* being released and achieving state-of-the-art performance on a variety of benchmarks. However, these models have yet to match the performance of closed, state-of-the-art models like GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. In this paper, we present Mistral AI 7B v0.1, an open-weight, open-source language model that uses only 8 billion parameters and performs on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks. Mistral AI 7B v0.1 is the first model released by Mistral AI, and we have made the weights and source code publicly available so that the community can build, study, and improve upon it. We hope that our model will be used to advance the field of open-source language models and provide a valuable resource for researchers and developers.

We believe that our model will be particularly useful for the following reasons: (1) It is open-source, which allows for easy customization and fine-tuning for specific use cases. (2) It is efficient, which makes it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. (3) It is designed with a focus on providing high-quality, factually accurate outputs, and avoiding harmful content, which makes it a safe and reliable tool for a wide range of applications. We are excited to see the ways in which the community will use and improve upon our model.

## 2 Related Work

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in open-source language models. One of the first open-source models, GPT-2 *(Radford et al., 2019)*, was released in 2019, and it has since been used for a wide variety of applications. Since then, a number of other open-source models have been released, including Llama *(Touvron et al., 2023)*, Vicuna *(Chiang et al., 2023)*, and OpenLLaMA *(Geng et al., 2023)*. These models have been used for a variety of tasks, including language translation, text summarization, and question answering. However, none of these models have yet to match the performance of closed, state-of-the-art models like GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.

In this section, we will review some of the most notable open-source language models that have been released in the past few years.

GPT-2 *(Radford et al., 2019)* is a transformer-based language model that was released in 2019. It has been used for a wide variety of applications, including language translation, text summarization, and question answering. GPT-2 has 1.5 billion parameters and was trained on a dataset of 40GB of text.

Llama *(Touvron et al., 2023)* is a dense model that was released in February 2023. It has 65 billion parameters and was trained on 1.4 trillion tokens of text. Llama was developed by researchers at Meta and it has been used for a variety of tasks, including language translation, text summarization, and question answering. Llama has been shown to perform on par with GPT-3 on a wide range of benchmarks.

Vicuna *(Chiang et al., 2023)* is a chat assistant that was released in March 2023. It has 7 billion parameters and was trained on 70,000 user-shared conversations collected from the ShareGPT website. Vicuna was developed by researchers at Berkeley AI Research (BAIR) and it has been shown to perform on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks.

OpenLLaMA *(Geng et al., 2023)* is a language model that was released in March 2023. It has 7 billion parameters and was trained on 1.1 trillion tokens of text. OpenLLaMA was developed by researchers at the University of Washington and it has been shown to perform on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks.

Mistral AI 7B v0.1 is the first model released by Mistral AI. It has 8 billion parameters and was trained on 1.2 trillion tokens of text. Mistral AI 7B v0.1 has been shown to perform on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks. We hope that our model will be used to advance the field of open-source language models and provide a valuable resource for researchers and developers.

## 3 Model

The architecture of the Mistral AI 7B v0.1 model is based on the transformer architecture *(Vaswani et al., 2017)*. The model has 8 billion parameters and 32 layers. Each layer consists of a self-attention mechanism and a feed-forward network. The self-attention mechanism allows the model to focus on specific parts of the input text, while the feed-forward network processes the information and generates the output.

The model was trained on a dataset of 1.2 trillion tokens of text. The dataset included a variety of text types, including books, articles, and web pages. The model was trained using the AdamW optimizer *(Loshchilov & Hutter, 2019)* with a learning rate of 6e-4 and a weight decay of 0.1. The training process took approximately 2 weeks on a cluster of 256 GPUs.

## 4 Evaluation

We evaluate Mistral AI 7B v0.1 on a variety of benchmarks to assess its performance on different tasks. The benchmarks include:

- LMSys Chatbot Arena *(Zheng et al., 2023)*: A human preference-based evaluation of chatbots.
- Open LLM Leaderboard *(Open LLM Leaderboard, 2023)*: A comprehensive evaluation of open-source language models on a wide range of tasks.
- Big-Bench Hard *(Suzgun et al., 2022)*: A challenging benchmark that consists of a diverse set of tasks that are designed to be difficult for language models.
- HumanEval *(Chen et al., 2021)*: A benchmark that consists of a set of programming problems that the model is asked to solve.
- MMLU *(Hendrycks et al., 2021)*: A benchmark that evaluates the model’s knowledge of various subjects.
- TruthfulQA *(Lin et al., 2022)*: A benchmark that evaluates the model’s ability to generate truthful answers to questions.

We compare Mistral AI 7B v0.1 to a number of closed, state-of-the-art models, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and PaLM. We also compare it to a number of open-source models, including Llama, Vicuna, and OpenLLaMA. The results of the evaluations are shown in Table 1.

In this paper, we presented Mistral AI 7B v0.1, an open-weight, open-source language model that uses only 8 billion parameters and performs on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks. We also released the weights and source code of the model so that the community can build, study, and improve upon it. While Mistral AI 7B v0.1 performs on par with GPT-3.5 on a wide range of benchmarks, it is still a relatively small model and may not be suitable for all applications. ## Game Mechanics

### Fighting System

Tekken 7's fighting system is a continuation of the series' traditional 3D fighting gameplay, with a few key additions. The game features a six-button control scheme, with three buttons for punches, three for kicks, and two directional inputs. Players can move around the stage freely, allowing for a wide range of movement and positioning options.

New to the series is the "Rage System," which activates when a player's health drops below a certain threshold. When activated, the character gains access to special moves that can turn the tide of the match. Additionally, the game introduces the "Counter System," which allows players to counter an opponent's attack by pressing a specific button at the right time.

The storyline of Tekken 7 revolves around the Mishima clan and their ongoing conflict. ## Methodology

In order to learn how to play Tekken 8, we first need to understand the game's mechanics and rules. We use Mistral-7B to process the game's data and extract relevant information.

### Understanding the Game

Tekken 8 is a fighting game where two characters face off against each other. Each character has a unique set of moves and abilities, and the goal is to deplete the opponent's health bar before they deplete yours. The game is played in rounds, and the first character to win two rounds wins the match.

### Data Extraction

We use Mistral-7B to process the game's data and extract the following information:

- Character information: Each character has unique statistics such as health, attack power, defense, etc. We extract these statistics for each character.
- Move information: Each character has a set of moves, including basic attacks, special moves, and throws. We extract the name, damage, and input of each move.
- Stage information: The game has various stages with different hazards and traps. We extract the name and description of each stage.

### Gameplay Mechanics

Once we have the game's data, we can begin to understand the game's mechanics. We use Mistral-7B to process this data and extract the following information:

- Combos: Combos are a sequence of moves that deal a significant amount of damage. We extract combos for each character and their damage output.
- Blocking: Blocking is a defensive move that prevents the opponent from dealing damage. We extract blocking frames for each move and use this information to develop blocking strategies.
- Movement: Movement is essential in Tekken 8. We extract movement frames for each character and use this information to develop movement strategies.

### Strategy Development

With the game's data and mechanics, we can begin to develop a strategy for playing the game. We use Mistral-7B to process this data and develop the following strategies:

- Matchup analysis: We analyze the strengths and weaknesses of each character and develop strategies to counter them.
- Stage selection: We select stages that favor our character and develop strategies to exploit the stage's hazards and traps.
- Adaptive gameplay: We develop strategies that adapt to the opponent's playstyle, such as switching between aggressive and defensive playstyles.

### Training

We use Mistral-7B to train the model to play the game. We use reinforcement learning to train the model to maximize its reward, which is defined as winning the match. We use the following algorithm:

- State: The current state of the game, including the health, position, and moves of both characters, and the stage.
- Action: The model chooses an action, which is a move or a movement input.
- Reward: The reward is based on the outcome of the action. If the action deals damage, the reward is positive. If the action is blocked, the reward is negative.
- Next state: The next state of the game after the action is taken.

- Discount factor: 0.99

- Number of epochs: 1000000

- Win rate: The percentage of matches the model wins against a set of opponents.
- Damage dealt: The average damage dealt per match.
- Block rate: The percentage of moves the model blocks.
